predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contract Completion Infeasibility Due to Capacity-Demand Imbalance
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project faces significant delivery risk as identified work volume substantially exceeds remaining capacity. With 15-23 sprints of work identified against 8.35 sprints remaining (1.8-2.8x overcapacity), combined with unfrozen MVP scope, pending architecture decisions, and declining delivery momentum, the December 31, 2026 contract end date cannot accommodate planned scope without extension or substantial reduction.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Combination of unfrozen MVP scope at 57% timeline completion, accumulation of post-MVP and pipeline work, pending architecture decisions consuming capacity, increasing rework (31.6% PR abandonment), and fixed contract end date with no documented extension mechanism.
triggerConditions: MVP scope remains unfrozen beyond September 2026
Architecture decisions (Snowflake write, integration testing, test data strategy) remain unresolved into October 2026
Sprint velocity continues declining due to production support and rework
Post-MVP scope planning continues without formal scope reduction or extension approval
Work-to-capacity ratio exceeds 2.0x by mid-October 2026

potentialImpact.schedule: Incomplete delivery by December 31, 2026; critical features deferred or cancelled; rushed final sprint execution compromising quality
potentialImpact.cost: Potential cost overrun if emergency extension negotiated; write-off of incomplete work; additional rework costs in subsequent contracts
potentialImpact.quality: Compressed delivery window forcing quality compromises; inadequate testing; technical debt accumulation; production stability risk
potentialImpact.customer: Unmet transformation objectives; stakeholder dissatisfaction; erosion of confidence in AI delivery capability; reluctance to approve future work
potentialImpact.operations: Incomplete operational readiness; inadequate documentation and knowledge transfer; support burden from rushed deployment; business continuity risk

supportingHistoricalPatterns: Historical Claims project experienced resource utilization risk when leadership decisions on FACETS integration were pending, blocking sprint readiness and creating capacity waste

Current project exhibits identical triggers: unfrozen MVP scope (risk opened 06/22/2026, ETA missed), multiple pending decisions, and work accumulation beyond available capacity

predictedRisks.reasoning: This risk is highly likely because the project has already consumed 57% of contract duration while critical scope and architecture decisions remain unresolved, creating a compounding delivery bottleneck. Historical evidence from the same client shows that decision latency and scope instability directly convert to utilization loss and schedule slippage. Current WSR metrics confirm declining momentum (increasing PR abandonment 1→4→6, declining contribution, 4 spilled PBIs) while work identification continues (pipeline items, post-MVP scope). The mathematical impossibility of fitting 15-23 sprints into 8.35 remaining sprints, combined with no documented extension mechanism and a hard December 31 end date, makes incomplete delivery the most probable outcome without immediate corrective action.

actions: Freeze MVP scope with formal stakeholder sign-off and enforce change control requiring executive approval for any additions
Negotiate 3-month contract extension to Q1 2027 or execute formal scope reduction reducing identified work to 8 sprints maximum
Re-baseline sprint commitments to 80% of demonstrated velocity to improve reliability and reduce spillover
Prioritize and sequence remaining work into must-have (MVP completion), should-have (critical post-MVP), and defer categories with client approval
Defer all pipeline work (AI Trust Office, Claims Use Case 8) to future contract or extension scope
Complete operational readiness activities (documentation, runbooks, KT) by December 15 to enable controlled closure

recommendations.preventive: Establish weekly work-to-capacity tracking with executive visibility and enforce scope freeze through formal change control requiring impact assessment and trade-off decisions for any new requests.
recommendations.strategic: Implement rolling 3-sprint lookahead planning with dependency mapping to identify capacity bottlenecks early and enable proactive mitigation.

predictedRisks.responseRationale: Historical Claims project demonstrated that decision escalation combined with alternate work preparation successfully resolved utilization risk when leadership decisions were pending, proving that proactive scope control and extension negotiation can prevent delivery failure under capacity constraints.
